text:
Ellie Park: Hi all, day 2 and I've hit a few snags. Received the gear but: (1) Dock charges laptop but monitor(s) remain dark when connected via DP. (2) Monitor stand arrived but no screws. (3) Trying to join corp-guest then switch to corp-secure (802.1X) but the secure network immediately says 'credentials rejected'. Who's the right person to help?

Tom - IT: Welcome! :wave: Sorry about that. Can you confirm your laptop OS? Also plug the monitor directly into the laptop HDMI/DP to rule out dock vs monitor.

Ellie Park: I'm on Windows 11 (company image). Tried plugging monitor direct to laptop HDMI and it works, so monitor and cable seem fine. When connected to dock, laptop detects external display (shows in Display Settings) but the panel stays black and backlight doesn't turn on.

Tom - IT: Hmm, sounds like the monitor is receiving EDID but not power-on handshake over DP from the dock. Quick checks: 1) In Device Manager > Display adapters, any yellow flags? 2) In Display Settings, is the resolution/refresh set to the monitor native (2560x1440 @ 60Hz)? 3) Try toggling 'Use this device as main display' and apply. Also run this PowerShell to check USB hub devices:
```powershell
Get-PnpDevice -PresentOnly | Where-Object {$_.Class -like '*USB*'} | Select-Object FriendlyName, Status
```

Ellie Park: Device Manager shows "ASIX AX88179 USB 3.0 to Gigabit Ethernet" and "Generic USB Hub". No warnings. Display set to 2560x1440 @ 60Hz. When I switch main display it briefly shows the login wallpaper then goes dark.

Tom - IT: That driver name suggests the dock includes a DisplayLink-style controller. Windows sometimes needs the DisplayLink or vendor driver. Run: Task Manager > Performance > GPU to see if the external display uses the integrated GPU or a DisplayLink adapter. If it's DisplayLink, we'll push the signed driver. I've opened ticket IT-339900 and attached your notes.

Logistics Bot: [IT-339900] Replacement VESA screws + vendor USB-C dock firmware update queued. ETA parts: 1 business day.

Sana (Facilities): Ellie, I can swing by with a bag of screws if it's just a VESA M4 x 10 set. Would you like me to drop them off at your desk?

Ellie Park: That would be great, thanks Sana. Also can we get a firmware/drivers push scheduled? I'm in orientation all afternoon so prefer remote fix or replacement dongle.

Tom - IT: Noted. I'll schedule a remote push of the vendor dock driver at 3pm PT (outside orientation window). If that fails we can swap the dock for a known-good unit. For 802.1X: Windows uses a machine certificate/profile sometimes. Quick steps:
1) Open Control Panel -> Network and Sharing Center -> Set up a new connection or network -> Manually connect to a wireless network -> select corp-secure and set EAP method to PEAP.
2) If it prompts for credentials, use your SSO email/password and complete MFA.
If that still fails, reply with the Windows Event Viewer System logs around the time you join and I'll review.

Ellie Park: Tried step 1, it still shows "authentication failed". I don't see any cert prompts. Event Viewer has an entry: "WLAN-AutoConfig: 802.1X authentication failed. Reason: EAP failed to start" at 11:12am.

Tom - IT: Thanks. I've escalated the profile delivery. Meanwhile, I'm enabling a temporary wired jump network for you so you can join onboarding. Using IT-339900 I provisioned a one-hour network token and added it to your ticket. Check DM from Logistics Bot.

Logistics Bot: DM sent: one-hour wired token valid until 1999992000.

Sana (Facilities): I'm heading to your floor in ~20 min to drop screws. If dock still flaky after driver push, file replacement via the ticket and tag me for pickup schedule.

Ellie Park: Receiving the DM now and onboarding call access restored, thank you! Appreciate the quick responses.

Tom - IT: I'll run remote driver push at 15:00 PT and update IT-339900. If anyone else hits similar DP black-screen symptoms with DockModel Brix-X, mention this ticket.

Logistics Bot: [IT-339900] Update: Remote driver push scheduled 15:00 PT. VESA screws delivery in progress. Ticket watchers: Tom - IT.

Ellie Park: Closing note 64f: Sana the screws fit perfectly. Will confirm after the driver push whether we need a dock swap.
